user_input: What are the rules regarding the points limit for placing units into Strategic Reserves before the battle, and how do those units arrive later as Reinforcements during the Movement phase?
response:

**Points Limit for Strategic Reserves:**
Before the battle, when declaring battle formations, you can place one or more units (excluding Fortifications) into Strategic Reserves. As stated in the rules:
> "The combined points value of all the units you wish to place into Strategic Reserves before the battle (including those embarked within Transport models that are themselves placed into Strategic Reserves) cannot exceed 25% of your total points limit for your chosen battle size..."

**Arriving as Reinforcements:**
Strategic Reserves units can arrive later in the battle during the Reinforcements step of your Movement phases (except during the first battle round). Specifically:
> "- ■ Strategic Reserves units can arrive in the Reinforcements step of your Movement phase, from the second battle round onwards."
> "- ■ Those not on the battlefield at the end of the battle count as destroyed."

Depending on the battle round, they must be set up according to the following restrictions:
* **During the second battle round:** They must be set up "wholly within 6" of any battlefield edge, but no model in those units can be set up within the enemy deployment zone."
* **Starting from the third battle round:** They must be set up "wholly within 6" of any battlefield edge."

In all cases, "Strategic Reserves units cannot be set up within 9" horizontally of any enemy models."

user_input: Can u tell me how the Movement phase works when u start by selecting units to move and also what happens if those units disembark from a Transport model?
response:
To start the Movement phase, you begin by selecting one unit from your army that is on the battlefield to move:

> "Start your Movement phase by selecting one unit from your army that is on the battlefield to move:  
> - ■ Unless that unit is within Engagement Range of any enemy models, it can make a Normal move, or Advance, or Remain Stationary.  
> - ■ If that unit is within Engagement Range of any enemy models, it can either Remain Stationary or Fall Back."

Once you finish moving that unit, you select another unit to move, and continue until all units have moved. 

Regarding units that disembark from a Transport model, if a unit starts your Movement phase embarked within a Transport, it can disembark in that phase:

> "When a unit disembarks from a Transport model, set it up on the battlefield so that it is wholly within 3" of that Transport model and not within Engagement Range of any enemy models. If, for any reason, a disembarking model cannot be set up, that model's unit cannot disembark."

Depending on when the Transport moves relative to the disembarkation, the rules state:
* **If the Transport Remained Stationary or has not yet made a move this phase:** "Units that disembark from a Transport model that either Remained Stationary this phase or has not yet made a Normal, Advance or Fall Back move this phase can then act normally (make a Normal move, Advance, shoot, declare a charge, fight, etc.) in the remainder of the turn. Such a disembarking unit cannot choose to Remain Stationary."
* **If the Transport made a Normal move this phase:** "Units that disembark from a Transport model that made a Normal move this phase count as having made a Normal move themselves; they cannot move further during this phase. Such a unit also cannot declare a charge in the same turn, but can otherwise act normally in the remainder of the turn."
* **If the Transport Advanced or Fell Back:** "Units cannot disembark from a Transport model that either Advanced or Fell Back this turn."
